text:
Recent work favors claim-level evidence checks over fluent explanations or semantic similarity. *On the Factual Consistency of Text-based Explainable Recommendation Models* (2025; revised 2026) extracts atomic statements and evaluates factual support and relevance, finding that strong similarity scores can coexist with poor factual precision. Its review-derived evidence is unavailable here; the transferable principle is linking each judgment to supplied evidence, not importing review-based labels. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24366)

Annotation disagreement also needs preservation. *Diverging Preferences* (2024–2026) distinguishes underspecification, style differences, refusals and annotation errors; conventional preference models and LLM judges can collapse divergent preferences into an apparently definitive winner. *Abstain-QA* (2025) separately evaluates answerable and unanswerable cases, supporting explicit assessment of insufficient evidence. These are adjacent evaluation findings, not validated recommendation-specific annotation protocols. [Disagreement study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14632), [Abstention study](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.627/)

Practical synthesis: annotate each actual user–recommendation pair with the explicit feedback span, relevant title/description evidence and timestamp. Separate documented requirement violations, supported compatibility, explicitly satisfied needs and precise preference matches; retain unknown/insufficient-evidence judgments separately. Missing item information cannot establish incompatibility, and interaction history alone cannot establish an explicit need or rejection. Measure preferred-over-rejected ordering only for explicitly comparable pairs; report ties and unknowns separately, alongside assessability coverage and pair counts. Use independent double annotation, nominal Krippendorff’s alpha or Cohen’s kappa, raw agreement and adjudication records. Treat these measures as diagnostic evidence alongside the fixed validation HR@10, not substitutes for it.
